messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: continuous-batching latency spike detected on prod (region-us-east-1). Severity P2. Auto-escalation to oncall-sre. traces: https://internal.redwood/tools/traces/3200004321

maria: seeing a huge queue buildup on cb-worker-12, queue depth jumped from ~10 to >1200 in 2m. CPU ok but tail latencies for sampling are through the roof.

aj: on it. grabbing recent metrics. are we seeing KV cache evictions at the same time?

sahil: yes, eviction rate spikes correlate with the queue. likely a prefix-KV regen loop. I can tail logs.

ops-bot: Deployment alert: rollback candidate 2026-03-12T03:41Z flagged for canary anomalies (cb-config v2.4.1).

maria: @sahil please post the top 5 logs you see, want to confirm any OOMs or repeated cache misses.

sahil: logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-12T03:40:21Z [cb-worker-12] INFO incoming_batch size=1024 requests=18 seq_len=256
2026-03-12T03:40:22Z [kv-cache] WARN eviction_rate=0.89 misses=738 repop_ms=1202
2026-03-12T03:40:23Z [cb-runtime] ERROR enqueue_delay_ms=4500 microbatch_size=64 jitter=0.02
2026-03-12T03:40:24Z [cb-worker-12] INFO continuous_batch_flush duration_ms=3900
```

aj: eviction rate almost 90% — that's extremely high. microbatch_size at 64 but incoming batch=1024 means continuous batching is trying to pack a lot and KV hot keys are cycling.

taylor: any customer-facing impact? product-ops: we're seeing a few high-priority customers in us-east with timeouts on chat-generation API; support already opened two SEV tickets.

maria: root cause hypothesis: a sudden traffic pattern increased concurrency and sequence length distribution, which caused continuous batching to grow request windows, increasing KV cache churn and triggering long repop times -> tail latencies -> queue pileup.

aj: action list: 1) apply emergency throttle to the continuous-batching controller on us-east 2) reduce microbatch_size to 16 3) enable conservative prefetch (disable aggressive prefetch) 4) push a hotfix rollback of cb-config v2.4.1 to v2.4.0 on canaries if safe.

sahil: I can change microbatch_size and prefetch on the running config via /deployctl -c cb-controller apply --patch. prepping commands.

maria: do we want to do a global change or region-limited? Prefer region-limited to us-east only.

aj: region-limited. publish the change to the controller in canary first then scale to the region. low-risk config tweak.

ops-bot: Command executed by sahil: `/deployctl -c cb-controller --region us-east patch --set microbatch_size=16 --set prefetch=conservative`

maria: confirmed canary change applied to cb-worker-2 and cb-worker-3. monitoring.

aj: metrics update: queue depth down to ~300 in 90s, eviction_rate down to 0.22, repop_ms back under 200. tail latency 95p improved from 9s -> 1.1s. nice.

taylor: support: informing customers in the two SEV tickets that we're mitigating and ETA ~15m. please add a brief RCA note once stable.

sahil: rolling the same config to remaining us-east nodes now. doing a staggered patch: workers 4..20.

maria: also toggling the continuous-batching admission throttle to cap in-flight microbatches to reduce buildup while we finish rollout. command: `rbctl set admission.cb_max_inflight 300 --region us-east`

ops-bot: Command executed by maria: `rbctl set admission.cb_max_inflight 300 --region us-east`

aj: after throttle, overall throughput dropped ~12% but latency stabilized — acceptable tradeoff for now.

product-ops: can we do a temporary traffic routing to other regions for affected customers? cross-region fallbacks are enabled but some customers are pinned by account. coordinating with sales.

maria: next steps: 1) finish rollout in us-east 2) hold cb-config v2.4.1 from further promotion until we run a synthetic with high concurrency and long seq lengths 3) open a formal incident ticket with timeline and customer impact 4) followup RCA on root cause (config vs workload shift)

aj: I'm creating the incident ticket now: INC-3200004321. assigning owners: mitigation=maria, rollback=sahil, customer-comm=taylor.

maria: happy path looks good. keep monitoring for 30m then close oncall handoff. thanks all. :thumbsup:
